Aymara ( Aymara pronunciation: [ajˈmaɾa] ⓘ ; also Aymar aru ) is an Aymaran language spoken by the Aymara people of the Bolivian Andes . It is one of only a handful of Native American languages with over one million speakers. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Aymara, along with Spanish and Quechua , is an official language in Bolivia and Peru . [ 4 ] It is also spoken, to a much lesser extent, by some communities in northern Chile and northern Argentina , where it is a recognized minority language .
